Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An exhaust treatment system and method for the treatment of an exhaust stream from a combustion engine are provided. A first oxidation of compounds comprising one or more of nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen in the exhaust stream is carried out by a first oxidation catalyst. Further, a value (NO2_1/NOx_1)det for a ratio between a first amount of nitrogen dioxide and a first amount of nitrogen oxides leaving said first oxidation catalyst is determined. Active control of at least one parameter related to the combustion engine is carried out, based on the determined value, so that the ratio is impacted. A first additive is supplied into the exhaust stream, following which a first reduction of the first amount of nitrogen oxides is carried out through a catalytic reaction in a catalytic filter, which consists of a particulate filter with an at least partly catalytic coating with reduction characteristics. The catalytic filter is arranged for catching and oxidizing of soot particles, and to carry out the first reduction of the first amount of nitrogen oxides using the first additive.

outputs.L1: An exhaust treatment system and method are provided for treating an exhaust stream from a combustion engine. A first oxidation catalyst performs a first oxidation of compounds in the exhaust stream comprising one or more of nitrogen, carbon, and hydrogen. A value, (NO₂_1/NOₓ_1)det, representing the ratio between a first amount of nitrogen dioxide and a first amount of nitrogen oxides leaving the first oxidation catalyst, is then determined. Based on the determined value, at least one parameter associated with the combustion engine is actively controlled to influence the ratio. A first additive is subsequently supplied to the exhaust stream, after which a first reduction of the first amount of nitrogen oxides is performed through a catalytic reaction in a catalytic filter. The catalytic filter comprises a particulate filter having an at least partially catalytic coating with reduction characteristics and is configured to capture and oxidize soot particles and to perform the first reduction of the first amount of nitrogen oxides using the first additive.
outputs.L2: A system and process are disclosed for treating exhaust gas produced by a combustion engine. A first oxidation catalyst initially oxidizes exhaust constituents containing nitrogen, carbon, hydrogen, or any combination thereof. The system then determines a ratio value, (NO2_1/NOx_1)det, representing the first quantity of nitrogen dioxide relative to the first quantity of nitrogen oxides exiting the oxidation catalyst. Based on this value, at least one engine-related operating parameter is actively adjusted to influence the ratio. A first additive is subsequently introduced into the exhaust stream. The first quantity of nitrogen oxides is then reduced through a catalytic reaction in a catalytic filter. This filter comprises a particulate filter having a coating that is at least partially catalytic and has reduction properties. It is configured both to capture and oxidize soot particles and, with the first additive, to perform the first reduction of nitrogen oxides.
outputs.L3: An exhaust-gas treatment system includes a first oxidation catalyst configured to oxidize exhaust compounds containing nitrogen, carbon, and/or hydrogen. The system determines the ratio of nitrogen dioxide to the total amount of nitrogen oxides in the exhaust gas leaving the first oxidation catalyst. Based on the determined ratio, the system actively controls at least one operating parameter of the combustion engine to influence and regulate that ratio. A first additive is then introduced into the exhaust stream to promote the reduction of nitrogen oxides. Downstream, a catalytic particulate filter captures and oxidizes soot particles while using the introduced additive to facilitate the reduction of nitrogen oxides.
outputs.L4:
An exhaust-treatment system for an internal-combustion engine is configured to remove both particulate matter and nitrogen oxides from the exhaust gas. Exhaust leaving the engine first passes through an oxidation device that oxidizes nitrogen-, carbon-, and hydrogen-containing exhaust constituents. For example, the device may convert at least part of the nitrogen monoxide to nitrogen dioxide while also oxidizing carbon monoxide and unburned hydrocarbons. A sensor located downstream of the oxidation device determines the concentration of nitrogen dioxide relative to the total concentration of nitrogen oxides, thereby providing a measured NO₂-to-NOx ratio.

A controller receives the sensor signal and compares the measured ratio with a desired value or operating range. When the ratio deviates from the target, the controller actively changes one or more engine operating parameters to alter the composition and temperature of the exhaust. Such changes may include adjustments to fuel injection timing or quantity, air supply, exhaust-gas recirculation, boost pressure, or other combustion-related settings. By regulating engine operation in this manner, the system maintains an exhaust composition favorable to both soot oxidation and NOx reduction.

An additive is introduced into the exhaust upstream of a particulate filter having catalytic NOx-reduction capability. Depending on the system configuration, the additive may function as a reducing agent, a reduction-agent precursor, or another material that promotes the desired catalytic reactions. The particulate filter traps soot and other solid particles while its catalytic coating supports reactions that convert nitrogen oxides into less harmful products. The controlled amount of nitrogen dioxide assists in oxidizing the accumulated soot, including during passive or actively managed filter regeneration, while the injected additive supports the simultaneous reduction of NOx.

Coordinating oxidation, NO₂-to-NOx measurement, engine control, additive dosing, filtration, and catalytic reduction allows the system to balance competing exhaust-treatment requirements. As a result, the particulate filter can be regenerated more effectively without sacrificing NOx-conversion performance, providing improved simultaneous removal of particulate matter and nitrogen oxides over a range of engine operating conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a combustion-engine exhaust aftertreatment method involving an oxidation catalyst, active engine control, additive injection, soot oxidation, and NOx reduction.
counterfactuals.output: A method for treating exhaust gas from a combustion engine includes passing the exhaust gas through an oxidation catalyst and actively controlling at least one engine operating parameter to adjust an exhaust-gas temperature, oxygen concentration, or nitrogen-oxide content. An additive is selectively injected into the exhaust stream upstream of an aftertreatment device to promote oxidation of soot accumulated on a particulate filter. During a soot-regeneration phase, the oxidation catalyst converts at least a portion of hydrocarbons and carbon monoxide and facilitates formation of an oxidizing species effective to oxidize the accumulated soot. During a nitrogen-oxide-reduction phase, engine operation and additive injection are coordinated to establish conditions favorable for reducing NOx in a downstream reduction catalyst. A controller determines catalyst and filter states from sensed or modeled operating parameters and controls engine operation, additive quantity, injection timing, and phase sequencing to achieve soot oxidation and NOx reduction while limiting fuel consumption, emissions, and excessive aftertreatment temperatures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an exhaust treatment system in which the NO₂-to-NOx ratio downstream of a first oxidation catalyst is measured and used to adjust engine operating parameters before selective catalytic reduction in a coated particulate filter.
counterfactuals.output:
An exhaust treatment system may include, in sequence:

1. **A diesel or lean-burn engine** having electronically controllable operating parameters, such as fuel-injection timing, injection quantity, exhaust-gas recirculation (EGR), boost pressure, and post-injection.
2. **A first oxidation catalyst** positioned downstream of the engine. The catalyst oxidizes CO and hydrocarbons and converts part of the engine-out NO to NO₂.
3. **An exhaust-sensing arrangement** downstream of the oxidation catalyst that determines total NOx and NO₂, directly or by combining multiple sensor signals or a sensor signal with an exhaust model. A controller calculates the ratio  
   \[
   R=\frac{[NO_2]}{[NO]+[NO_2]}.
   \]
4. **A reductant delivery device**, such as a urea-water injector, located downstream of the ratio-measurement location.
5. **A particulate filter coated with an SCR catalyst** downstream of the injector. The filter traps soot while the SCR coating uses ammonia derived from the reductant to reduce NO and NO₂ to nitrogen.

The controller compares the measured NO₂-to-NOx ratio with a target ratio selected according to exhaust temperature, flow, catalyst state, soot loading, and requested NOx conversion. If the ratio differs from the target, the controller changes one or more engine operating parameters. For example, it may alter EGR rate, air-fuel ratio, boost, main-injection timing, or late/post-injection to change engine-out NOx composition, exhaust temperature, and oxidation-catalyst activity. It may also coordinate these changes with reductant dosing.

Maintaining a suitable NO₂ fraction—often near the proportion favorable for fast SCR—improves NOx conversion in the SCR-coated particulate filter, supports passive soot oxidation, and avoids excessive NO₂ slip or undesirable particulate-filter regeneration behavior. The control may operate in closed loop and may include sensor plausibility checks, catalyst-temperature limits, and fallback model-based control.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical abstract for an invention that treats diesel exhaust by oxidizing nitrogen-, carbon-, or hydrogen-containing compounds, determining the outlet NO₂/NOx ratio, controlling combustion based on that ratio, injecting a reductant, and reducing NOx while trapping soot.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system are provided for treating exhaust from a diesel combustion engine. The exhaust is passed through an oxidation catalyst configured to oxidize one or more nitrogen-, carbon-, or hydrogen-containing compounds, including conversion of at least a portion of nitric oxide to nitrogen dioxide. A sensing or estimation system determines a ratio of nitrogen dioxide to total nitrogen oxides in exhaust leaving the oxidation catalyst. An engine controller adjusts one or more combustion parameters based on the determined ratio to maintain conditions favorable for downstream emissions treatment. A reductant is introduced into the exhaust downstream of the oxidation catalyst, and the resulting mixture is directed through an emissions-control device configured to selectively reduce nitrogen oxides while trapping particulate matter, including soot. Coordinated control of combustion, reductant delivery, nitrogen-oxide reduction, and particulate capture improves exhaust purification over varying engine operating conditions.
